long_biography.plain_text:
Reviving Serbian sugar production became the defining industrial achievement of Miodrag Kostić's MK Group. Beginning with refinery acquisitions in 2002, he built Sunoko into a regional sugar producer, then added agricultural companies and Carnex, using investment and digitalisation to deepen the group's food-production base.

Beyond food production, the portfolio grew through banking, Adriatic hotels and Serbia's early wind farms. Kostić withdrew from management in 2019, entrusting strategic leadership to his son Aleksandar and executive control to professional teams. His final large public project was the Palace of Science in Belgrade, created through his endowment as a centre for research, education and scientific outreach.

MK Group's official obituary establishes death on 13 November 2024. The mortality status is corrected, but the inventory categorises the blank death-day, month and year fields as inapplicable or system-managed, so no proposals are made for those fields.

Kostić was a founder-operator for most of his career, but the classification describes his position at death: ultimate ownership remained documented while strategy and management had been delegated for approximately five years. Passive asset owner therefore outranks Founder for the terminal relationship field without diminishing his founder history.

Food manufacturing captures the sugar and branded-food platform that materially built Kostić's wealth, while Banking captures his directly documented ultimate ownership of AIK Bank.
